newsitem.title: UK: Zaire's Tenke feasability study seen by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Tenke feasability study seen by year-end.

text.p: The feasibility study on the giant Tenke Fungurume copper/cobalt deposit in Zaire is expected to be completed by the end of 1997, Brian Spratley, Technical director of Mining Development Services Ltd (MDS) said.
MDS says work is normal at the site despite civil war.
MDS is a subsidiary company of Canada's Tenke Mining Corp, who are developing a vast mine in the mineral-rich Shaba province after signing a deal with Zaire's government last December.
The project, the first major foreign investment in Zaire since the 1970s, is a joint-venture with state-owned Gecamines who have a 45 percent holding.
"We aim to complete it (the study) by the end of the year...It is costing $22 million," Spratley said at a presentation to the Association of Mining Analysts (AMA).
Mineral reserves at the deposit are estimated at 93 million tonnes, grading at 4.59 percent copper and 0.37 percent cobalt, he said.
Tenke's intention is to start up copper production by mid-2000 at an initial rate of 100,000 tonnes a year, working up to 400,000 tonnes annually.
Cobalt production will be 8,000 tonnes, or some 25 percent of the current world market, Spratley said.
Tenke will produce London Metal Exchange (LME) Grade A copper cathodes and vacuum degassed cobalt cathodes of 99.5 percent purity or better.

Production costs are estimated at $0.39/lb and $1.50/2.00/lb for copper and cobalt respectively. Tenke is currently projecting revenue reference prices of $0.85/lb and $8.00/lb for its copper and cobalt.
